anti_overlap: fd-emergence-systems-coherence covers whether the simulation produces good outputs to observe
fd-shadow-org-loop covers whether the deployment mechanic is mechanically sound
decision_lens: Every finding is prioritized by whether it affects the critical first 2 minutes: 'a player generates a world and within 2 minutes sees events appearing.' The no-tutorial bet requires the legible-world layer to work exceptionally well.
focus: Whether the 'no tutorial, legible world, opaque systems' philosophy is achievable in practice and will produce self-selected audience, rather than mass bounce-off
name: fd-player-psychology-onboarding
persona: A UX researcher and game designer who studied how players learn Dwarf Fortress, Factorio, and Crusader Kings II — specifically the cognitive models players build during their first 30 minutes, and which design decisions separate 'hard but fair' from 'unnecessarily opaque.'
review_areas: Audit 'legible world, opaque systems' against concrete UI elements — does the event feed, pressure dashboard, and issue cards give clear 'what is happening' signals within 2 minutes?
Examine the 'no tutorial' bet against genre comparisons — DF has the wiki, Factorio has progressive unlocking; what is Shadow Work's equivalent legibility scaffolding?

Analyze target audience ('people who read geopolitics for fun') against required cognitive model — understanding geopolitics is not the same as understanding pressure cascades; does domain knowledge transfer?
Check 'consequences not judgments' against the success criterion — 'player develops a theory and tests it' requires hypothesis formation from observing consequences without guidance
Evaluate the scenario framing (15 custom descriptions for 5 issue types) — is this enough narrative surface area for the Prometheus scenario to feel distinct from generic sandbox?
Assess 'players who bounce are not the target audience' — is there a design intervention that preserves the no-tutorial ethos while reducing unnecessary bounce?
success_hints: A new player can describe what their shadow org is trying to accomplish within 5 minutes, even if they can't explain the pressure system
The game distinguishes 'you did that' (deployment consequences) from 'the world did this' (institutional agent actions) as readable signals
Players who bounce do so because complexity exceeds their interest, not because the UI failed to show them what to do
task_context: Shadow Work is a geopolitical simulation game with a Rust backend and React/Tauri UI, targeting a 'Prometheus Crisis' playable demo. PHILOSOPHY.md and VISION.md are the foundational design documents being reviewed.
